text:
The Blues beat New Jersey 9-6 on Saturday, which tells you most of what you need to know about their week: they've won three straight and scored 22 goals doing it. The chances behind that are ordinary, though. St. Louis had 51% of the expected goals in the streak (the quality of chances) and turned 12.3 expected goals into 22 real ones. That kind of finishing rarely holds.

The season picture is a team right on the line. The Blues are 12-9-2 with 49% of the expected goals and an even split at 5v5, our playoff odds are a coin flip at 44%, and their points almost exactly match their play.

The story is in net. Joel Hofer has a .933 save rate and 5.3 goals saved above expected over his last five starts; Jordan Binnington is at .844 and 3.9 goals worse than expected over his. Binnington's name has been in trade talk, and the headlines now ask whether his play has cooled that market.

Up front, Jimmy Snuggerud is on pace to be the first Blue to score 40 since Vladimir Tarasenko, per The Hockey News, on a top line with Robert Thomas and Dylan Holloway that has played 205 minutes together. The blue line is chipping in, too: Justin Barron has 8 points in 10 games (4.1 expected) and Logan Mailloux 7 in 6 (2.7). Both are running well ahead of their chances.
